label: text
text: "Serious objections" by the "chief "at" application made on behalf of the Cafe Parisien "were mentioned at "to-day's Licensing Sessions."

label: text

The application, which was for
a. I'dificant's licence, without Bar,

label: text

label: text
text: The Hon. Mr. W. T. Southern, Chairman of the Licensing Board, said that the best course would be to discuss the matter at the conclusion of other Business when he would request the Press to withdraw. In any event, the application would not be granted at that session as the Cafe management had written withdrawing the application.

label: text

A Treasury Loss.
Arising out of the application on behalf of Lane, Crawford's Cafe for a Publions licence with: Bar, the Chairman said that he understood that an adjunct licence only had been held previously. He asked for the exact direction.

label: text
text:
War I had sometimes been the
ake that holders of adjunct li-
ences practised as if they held
the full licence, buyers of a sand-
wich at almost any hour being
provided with drinks.
It was to prevent this loss to the Treasury that the regulations with regard to limitation of the hours in which an adjunct licence applied (from 12.30 to 2.30, the tiffin hour, and 6 p.m. to 9 p.m.) had been introduced.
In this particular case, the holding of a full licence would enable Lane Crawford's Cafe to sell at any time from 8 a.m. to midnight. It enabled them, for instance, to provide liquor during dinner dances. Customers could go in at any time during the hours specified and ask for a whiskey soda, glass of sherry, etc. It applied in the same way as that of the Hong Kong Hotel lounge.

label: text
text: The full licence had already been provisionally granted for two months, said Mr. Wolfe.

label: text
text: MAUSERS WORTH $20,000

label: text
text: SEIZURE ON "COBLENTZ."

label: text
text: One of the largest seizures of arms and ammunition made in recent months took place on Wednesday evening, when officers of the Re-

label: text
text: Norddeutscher-Lloyd s.s.,"Coblentz" 5,393 tons (Capt. W. Heher), upon her arrival in port from Continental porta via Singapore.

label: text
text: Acting upon information received, Revenue Officers went straight to the vessel's forecast where twenty racks, all now, were found in apparent readiness to be moved over board.

label: text
text: These sacks were forthwith seized by the Revenue Officers participating in the search and, upon examination, were found to contain 140 Mauser pistols and no less than 18,000 rounds of ammunition. Up to the time of going to press no arrest had been made. The "Coblentz" sailed for Shanghai and Northern ports at daylight yesterday.

label: text
text: A conservative estimate places the value of n Mauser pistol with 100 rounds, once in China, at $150, so that the haul would represent about $20,000.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON'S BOYCOTT.

label: text
text: Transport “Severance”

label: text
text: CORPS OF LADY SEARCHES.

label: text
text: Views on British Goods Being

label: text
text: Hong Kong's steamboat companies have not been officially informed to do cargo will not be handled at Canton as from Monday, Nov. 8.

label: text
text: As reported in yesterday's "China Mail," the Transport Union passed a resolution to the effect that British goods would be boycotted from the date mentioned.

label: text
text: Local Chinese firms, however, have been instructed by connections in Canton, not to ship up, any cargo after to-morrow as there will be no "sampans or coolies" to land merchandise from Hong Kong.

label: text
text: The boats will continue to carry cargo if forthcoming and it remains to be seen if the threat will be carried out on Monday.

label: text
text: Blind Girl Pickets?

label: text
text: The latest development in the "severance of economic relations" movement is the formation of a body of lady searchers.

label: text
text: Mrs. Ho Heung-ying (wife of Liao Chung-kai, the Labour Minister assassinated last year) is the

label: text
text: Mrs. Ho Heung-ying who is also official head of the Kuomintang Women's Department.

label: text
text: leader. She called a meeting on Wednesday and about 200 of the fair sex were present, comprising mostly students, waitresses, domestic servants, women of suspicious character and a few blind girls!

label: text
text: Thirty patrols of six each were formed and a detachment proceeded forthwith to the city.

label: text
text: Shops were searched, principals were questioned as to the stocks of British cargo carried and the women remained for several hours.

label: text
text: Moderation in Views.

label: text
text: There are now only about 1,000 strike pickets left in Canton. A good many have been embodied in the Government Inspection Corps to carry out examination of shipping. The remainder are at Tung Yuen (headquarters), Fong Chuen and East Parade ground. A proposal is on foot to remove the whole batch to Bocca. Tigris for training, the nature of which has not been specified.

label: text
text: Shopkeepers who are members of the Association to Sever Relations are moderating their views. Resolutions have been passed forbidding pickets, searchers and their fokis' union from entering business premises without permission.

label: text
text: There is little or no change to record in river shipping, the Steamboat Co.'s vessel being still avoided although the Canton Police are keeping the ex-seamen agitators away from the wharves in Canton.

label: paragraph_title
text: A NEW LEADER?

label: text
text:
RUMOURS ABOUT CHANG
KAI-SHEK.

label: text
text: SIGNIFICANT FACTORS.

label: text
text: General Li Lieh-chun, a non-Cantonese who was once chief-of-staff to the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen and who commanded the first band of Yunnanese mercenaries in Kwangtung province, passed through Hong Kong yesterday, on his way to Canton from Shanghai.

label: text
text: An unconfirmed report says that General Li was accompanied by Mr. Wang Ching-tiing (C. T. Wang) who was one of the three Chinese delegates to the Paris Peace Conference after the War

label: text
text: Mr. Wang has not been prominent in North China politics for a few years and is believed to have become a pronounced radi- al on joining the Kuomintang fold.

label: text
text: Attempts to interview General Li and Mr. Wang proved abortive as their movements were well concealed.

label: text
text: Considerable significance is attached to General Li's return to Canton.

label: paragraph_title
text: Crop of Reports.

label: text
text: After an unsuccessful bomb attempt on his life, pressure was brought to bear on him by the military faction then in power and he left the province.

label: text
text: About a month ago, he was appointed Nationalist commander in Kiangsi province.

label: text
text: Nothing developed and his arival in Canton is associated with the crop of reports of the death of General Chang Kai-shek, the ommander-in-chief.

label: text
text: Sources, which "believe in the rumour, on receipt of information from Shanghai, state emphatically that General Li has gone to Canton as the result of General Chang being "incapacitated through war wounds from further active service, and that General Li will be the new chief in the field.

label: paragraph_title
text: KIUKIANG TAKEN.

label: text
text: ALLIED BASE GONE!

label: text
text: British Naval Party Land on

label: text
text: Concessions

label: text
text: The greatest surprise of the present China War has been caused by the sudden capture of Kiukang by Canton's forces.

label: text
text: Two cables received to-day leave little room for doubt. They read:—

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, Nov. 5.

label: text
text: Southerners occupied Kiuklang yesterday.—Reuter.

label: text
text: At Kliukiang there was heavy firing around the foreign Concessions.

label: text
text: British Naval men were landed and everything is quiet at present.—Reuter.

label: text
text: How the Southerners accomplished the feat is at present a complete mystery.

label: text
text: Three or four weeks ago, they came very near to entering this most important base, the headquarters in the field of Marshal Sun Chuan-fang.

label: text
text:
Other Powers Also Land.
Trenches were dug, on the heights guarding the key to the river port and several determined Cantonese onslaughts were repulsed.

label: text
text: Although they had been in Te'an and Nanchang (both on the railway running inland from Kiukiang), the Nationalists had never indicated that Kiukiang was their goal.

label: text
text: A wireless report states that Naval detachments from the American and Japanese warships at Kiukiang were also landed on the Concession to keep order.

label: text
text:
Serious Northern Debacle.
Evidently, the Northerners were taken by surprise. Bearing in mind the incidents at Nanchang (which twice "fell" to the Southerners through "revolt"), it can only be surmised that treachery was partly, if not wholly, responsible for this most serious Northern debacle.

label: text
text: Lying as it does at a strategic point on the lower course of the Yangtse, Kiukiang bars the way of the Cantonese towards Shanghai and the Central China coast. The Southerners can now move on Anking (capital of Anhui) which is so close to Nanking (capital of Kiangsu and Marshal Sun's seat of government) as to predict great danger. Nanking is about 33 hours by rail from Shanghai! Earlier war news will be found on page 6 of this issue.
